instructions:
GOAL: Add the bespoke 5-stage Starting Adventure biomes — Grasslands, Forest, Cobblestone Path, Dungeon, Deep Dungeon — each with its OWN tileset and themed monsters. Extend the enemy rosters and per-zone stat profiles for the new biomes, make the floor renderer use each biome's real ground/wall TILE TEXTURES (falling back to a flat tint when a tile texture isn't real yet), skin the themed monsters, and add worldmap hexes for the new biomes. Deterministic sim.

IMPORTANT FILE-PATH NOTE: the header lists 'src/sim/spawn.ts'; the real file is 'src/sim/systems/spawn.ts' (ZONE_PROFILES lives there, not in a separate spawn.ts). ZONE_ROSTERS lives in 'src/sim/data/enemies.ts'. Edit those two. Renderer floor is in 'src/render/stage.ts' (Renderer.drawFloor + BIOME_PALETTES). Worldmap is 'src/render/worldmap.ts' (HEX_LIST).

GROUNDING (read before editing):
- src/sim/data/enemies.ts: ZONE_ROSTERS: Record<string, EnemyDef[]> keyed by zone name; each EnemyDef = { typeId, hp, radius, fast }. Existing zones: Forest, Ocean, Desert, Snow, Mountain, Ashen (typeId convention = `<zone>_<name>`, e.g. forest_sprite). DEFAULT_ROSTER (goblin/orc) is the null-zone fallback. NOTE: as of now spawnSystem does NOT actually read ZONE_ROSTERS to choose typeId — swarm enemies spawn generically as Kind.Enemy with zone-scaled hp/speed from ZONE_PROFILES, and the renderer skins every non-boss as 'enemy.grunt'. So to get THEMED monsters visible you must (a) tag spawned enemies with a zone typeId and (b) skin by that typeId in the renderer. Do both, minimally.
- src/sim/systems/spawn.ts: ZONE_PROFILES: Record<string, {hpMult, speedMult, themeTint}> keyed by zone name; NO_ZONE fallback. Entities carry `themeTint` (0..6). The swarm spawn block sets e.hp/e.speed/e.themeTint from ZONE_PROFILES[s.environmentType].
- src/render/stage.ts: Renderer.drawFloor(biome?) currently fills a tiled 32x32 floor + side wall columns using BIOME_PALETTES (a flat [floorBase, floorAlt, wallColor] per biome) via Graphics.rect(...).fill(color) — NO textures. drawFloor is called on init and re-called from sync() when s.environmentType changes (the `_lastBiome` guard). Non-boss enemies are skinned via Renderer.textureKeyForKind → always 'enemy.grunt'. environmentType is the hex `type` string set in src/main.ts startRun() from the selected hex.
- src/render/worldmap.ts: HEX_LIST is the array of hexes ({q,r,name,type,icon,color,description}). `type` is what becomes s.environmentType. Travel gating in _rebuildGrid uses hex distance from cleared hexes; hex (0,0) is always the free starting hex. To make the Starting Adventure reachable/orderable, the new biome hexes should form a connected chain from an existing/discoverable hex.
- Seeded art keys (getTexture auto-declares a placeholder if missing, so nothing breaks): tiles (32x32) tile.grass_ground / tile.grass_wall / tile.cobble_ground / tile.cobble_wall / tile.dungeon_ground / tile.dungeon_wall / tile.deep_ground / tile.deep_wall. Enemies: enemy.grass_boar, enemy.grass_wolf, enemy.cobble_bandit, enemy.cobble_archer, enemy.dungeon_skeleton, enemy.dungeon_bat, enemy.deep_wraith, enemy.deep_golem (Forest reuses existing enemy.forest_sprite / enemy.forest_treant if present, else the grunt fallback). To know whether a tile/enemy key is REAL vs placeholder, check src/assets/registry.ts getEntry(key)?.status === 'real'; getTexture always returns a usable texture regardless.

BIOME NAMING (pick canonical zone strings and use them consistently across all four files): use these exact `type` strings — 'Grasslands', 'Forest' (existing), 'Cobblestone', 'Dungeon', 'DeepDungeon'. The hex `type` in HEX_LIST, the ZONE_ROSTERS keys, the ZONE_PROFILES keys, and any renderer biome→tileset map MUST all use these identical strings.

DO THIS:

1. ENEMY ROSTERS (src/sim/data/enemies.ts): Add ZONE_ROSTERS entries (greybox stats, deterministic — no rng in this data):
   - Grasslands: [{typeId:'grass_boar', hp:24, radius:13, fast:false}, {typeId:'grass_wolf', hp:18, radius:12, fast:true}]
   - Cobblestone: [{typeId:'cobble_bandit', hp:26, radius:13, fast:false}, {typeId:'cobble_archer', hp:20, radius:12, fast:true}]
   - Dungeon: [{typeId:'dungeon_skeleton', hp:30, radius:13, fast:false}, {typeId:'dungeon_bat', hp:14, radius:10, fast:true}]
   - DeepDungeon: [{typeId:'deep_wraith', hp:34, radius:14, fast:true}, {typeId:'deep_golem', hp:80, radius:20, fast:false}]
   Forest already exists (forest_sprite/forest_treant) — reuse it, do not duplicate. Keep DEFAULT_ROSTER as-is.

2. ZONE PROFILES (src/sim/systems/spawn.ts): Add ZONE_PROFILES entries for the new biomes with distinct themeTint codes (these codes must be understood by the renderer's tint/skin map — see step 4; reuse an existing code if it maps to the right visual, or extend the mapping). Suggested: Grasslands {hpMult:0.9, speedMult:1.05, themeTint:<new>}, Cobblestone {hpMult:1.0, speedMult:1.0, themeTint:<new>}, Dungeon {hpMult:1.1, speedMult:0.95, themeTint:<new>}, DeepDungeon {hpMult:1.3, speedMult:1.0, themeTint:<new>}. If you add new themeTint numbers, update the Entity.themeTint comment in state.ts and any renderer tint table so the codes stay documented. Determinism: these are pure constants; the spawn block already applies them without rng beyond the existing fast-roll.

3. THEMED MONSTER TYPE TAGGING (src/sim/systems/spawn.ts + a tiny renderer wire): So the correct themed sprite can be chosen, tag each spawned swarm enemy with which roster entry it is. Minimal deterministic approach: in the swarm spawn block, after computing `fast`, look up `ZONE_ROSTERS[s.environmentType]` (import it from ../data/enemies); pick the roster entry by variant (fast → the entry with fast:true, else the fast:false entry; if the roster has both, this is a clean deterministic map — no rng needed beyond the existing fast roll). Store the chosen typeId on the entity so the renderer can skin it. Entity currently has no string typeId field; add `typeId: string` to the Entity interface in state.ts (default '' in makeEntity) and set it here (e.g. e.typeId = chosenDef.typeId). Leave boss/miniboss typeId '' (they skin by Kind). This adds one deterministic field; it does not affect the win-path math. If you prefer to avoid a string field on the hot Entity for perf, you MAY instead derive the typeId in the renderer purely from (environmentType, variant) via a lookup table — either is acceptable; the string field is simplest and clearest.

4. RENDER FLOOR = REAL TILES (src/render/stage.ts drawFloor): Add a biome→tileset map: BIOME_TILES: Record<string,{ground:string; wall:string}> = { Grasslands:{ground:'tile.grass_ground',wall:'tile.grass_wall'}, Cobblestone:{ground:'tile.cobble_ground',wall:'tile.cobble_wall'}, Dungeon:{ground:'tile.dungeon_ground',wall:'tile.dungeon_wall'}, DeepDungeon:{ground:'tile.deep_ground',wall:'tile.deep_wall'} } (Forest/others without seeded tiles keep the palette-tint path). In drawFloor(biome), if BIOME_TILES[biome] exists AND getEntry(groundKey)?.status === 'real' (tiles actually derived), render the floor and walls as TILED SPRITES using getTexture(groundKey)/getTexture(wallKey) instead of Graphics fills: build a tiling by placing 32x32 Sprites across the same -ext..+ext grid, or use a Pixi TilingSprite per region (ground region and the two wall columns) for far fewer objects — TilingSprite is preferred (one TilingSprite for the ground rect, one per wall column). Keep the same wall-column geometry (WALL_COLS width, ARENA extents) as the current Graphics version. FALLBACK: if BIOME_TILES lacks the biome OR the tile key isn't real yet (status !== 'real'), fall back to the existing BIOME_PALETTES flat-tint Graphics path so the floor always renders and the game never breaks. Keep drawFloor deterministic-render-safe (the existing cellHash variation can stay for the tint fallback; textured tiles don't need per-cell hashing). Ensure the floor scroll (`this.floor.y = (s.time*MAP_SCROLL_SPEED)%32`) still applies whether the floor is Graphics or TilingSprite (put the tiles in the same `this.floor` container or apply the same y).

5. RENDER THEMED ENEMIES (src/render/stage.ts): Extend enemy skinning to use the typeId. In spriteFor()/textureKeyForKind, when e.kind is a normal Enemy and e.typeId is a non-empty known key of the form '<biome>_<name>', use getTexture('enemy.'+e.typeId) (e.g. e.typeId 'grass_boar' → 'enemy.grass_boar'); if the derived key isn't real, getTexture returns a labeled greybox — acceptable fallback. Preserve the existing slot→Sprite reuse + re-skin-on-change logic (extend spriteKind tracking to also re-skin when the typeId key changes, not just Kind). Boss/MiniBoss keep their current Kind-based skins.

6. WORLDMAP HEXES (src/render/worldmap.ts HEX_LIST): Add hexes for the new biomes so the Starting Adventure is a connected, ordered chain and each biome is selectable. Reuse the existing (0,0) starting hex as Grasslands OR add Grasslands adjacent to it, then chain Forest → Cobblestone → Dungeon → DeepDungeon along adjacent hex coords so travel gating (distance-1 from a cleared hex) unlocks them in order. Give each a name/icon/color/description and set `type` to the exact canonical biome string ('Grasslands','Forest','Cobblestone','Dungeon','DeepDungeon'). Ensure the coords don't collide with existing hexes (existing used coords: (0,0),(1,-1),(0,1),(-1,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,0),(2,-1),(0,2)) — pick free adjacent coords. The DeepDungeon hex is the final stage (GDD final boss Skeleton Commander — boss identity is out of scope here; just place the hex).

DETERMINISM RULE (hard): sim edits (enemies.ts, spawn.ts, state.ts field) use only constants + s.rng / s.time / FIXED_DT. No new rng draws in the spawn path beyond the existing fast-roll (typeId selection is a pure function of variant, not a new draw). No Math.random / Date.now / performance.now / DOM in src/sim/. Renderer changes are presentation-only and must not mutate sim state.

ACCEPTANCE (worker must satisfy):
- DETERMINISTIC (sim tests / headless, fixed seed): (a) setting s.environmentType to each new biome spawns swarm enemies whose typeId belongs to that biome's ZONE_ROSTERS (assert every spawned normal enemy's typeId is one of the roster's two typeIds for that zone); (b) ZONE_PROFILES resolves for each new biome (hp/speed reflect the biome's mults, not NO_ZONE); (c) roster/profile resolution is byte-identical run-to-run for a fixed seed (existing determinism test stays green — the added typeId field must not change existing numeric outputs for existing zones).
- VISUAL (preview screenshot, per biome): selecting Grasslands/Cobblestone/Dungeon/DeepDungeon shows that biome's floor rendered with its TILE textures (not a flat tint) when the tiles are real, and the swarm shows that biome's themed monster sprites; a biome without real tiles still renders via the tint fallback. Worldmap shows the new biome hexes as a reachable ordered chain.
- GATE GREEN: sim imports no render; renderer never writes sim fields; the tile/enemy-key fallbacks keep the game rendering even when a key is still a placeholder.
